avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional land. Boroughs are adding their own resources: park fund money, equipment rentals, blue-collar worker teams. Exemptions also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its reserved fund for park purposes to buying trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with renovating the chalet in parc Pratt and redeveloping its surroundings, including planting vegetation, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees there for planting.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and mini-sweepers with operators to remove abrasives from streets, sidewalks and bike paths. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is also hiring a company to clean the sidewalks of four private snow removal sectors.

etapes.titre: Maintenance and snow removal of public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is hiring companies for the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six downtown squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

Montréal-Nord is paying for the rental of an additional grader for the 2025-2026 winter and Saint-Léonard is allocating $200,000 in surplus to its 2026 snow removal operations. Verdun is offering to supply the City with its own staff for its territory's snow disposal site for 2025, 2026 and 2027.

aSurveiller.texte: Extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
Snow removal of service roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest runs from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and starting work on its drinking water and sewer networks, in several boroughs and on main pipes. It is also continuing the wastewater disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte treatment plant and paying for the ongoing operation of this plant. Boroughs are taking charge of the replacement of lead water service connections, including the portion located on private land.

etapes.texte: The City awards contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining, without digging a trench, and to redo the roadway on various streets in many boroughs. These contracts include the replacement of lead water service connections on both the public and private sides.

etapes.titre: Lead water service connections on private land
etapes.texte: Boroughs offer city council the option of taking charge of the replacement of lead service connections located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the property owners concerned [CA26 22 0034].

The City awards contracts to rebuild water pipes and infrastructure along rue Guy and on rue De Champlain, and adds funds to the contracts for rue Saint-Antoine Ouest and rue de la Cathédrale. On rue De Champlain, the work replaces a 1,200 mm pipe installed in 1927 [CG26 0332].

The City renews or awards contracts to operate the wastewater treatment plant: process control system, chemicals, residue landfilling, cleaning services, upgrading of sludge incinerators, and mechanical work. The mechanical work is aimed in particular at reconditioning screens damaged during heavy rains [CG26 0543].

aSurveiller.texte: Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026, then of incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Adoption expected on October 19, 2026 of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
Rehabilitation work on the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord to be completed by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
End of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Rue Guy worksite expected to continue until December 2027; ozone plant commissioning expected in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park by phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrade.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward with several projects at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. It is launching construction of a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, replacing electrical equipment at the site, renewing park maintenance, and redeveloping rue De Louvain nearby. It is also requesting funding from the Québec government for a cycling and pedestrian link.

etapes.texte: The City is requesting financial assistance from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The file describes a 900-metre path through the park, including a footbridge of about 150 metres, and assistance of up to $2,000,000 [CG26 0121].

The City approves construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform, then hands the project over to the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The borough then awards a contract for $499,865.92, taxes included, to supply and install two greenhouses, with $74,979.88 in contingencies [CA26 14 0163].

The City awards a contract for $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, with $163,754.01 in contingencies. The work involves a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator, and a controller to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223].

The borough awards a contract of up to $8,199,514.82, taxes included, to redevelop rue De Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a total authorized expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, the bike path, and plantings [CA26 14 0076].

The City awards two companies contracts for general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028. It also extends the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ, and the soccer stadium by six months, for $193,215.49 more, taxes included [CG26 0521].

The City extends the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the complex by five months, for $296,349.21 more, taxes included; the compost is used in part to landscape the park [CG26 0320]. In October, the borough authorizes submitting a funding request to the Véloce III program for the bike lane and sidewalks on rue De Louvain Est.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is submitting its request, ends on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouse installation work must be completed by December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The extended snow removal contract covers November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs by unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, extra mortar, sod, and a deteriorated culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. Filing the application involves no spending; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural habitats
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are added to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération (Registry of natural habitats protected and contributing to biodiversity in the agglomeration), with conservation plans. The 2025 report filed shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, representing 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

A contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; the total expenditure reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow removal, cleaning and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the snow removal of service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors ($178,330.82, taxes included), and 9232-3914 Québec inc. the cleaning of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other dying trees in the park, for a total expenditure of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Cleaning of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension until October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and dying trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan filed in February 2027, DarkSky International's response expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

logement.description: Grants, land and projects for social, affordable or student housing, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: This year, the City is approving the 2026 budgets of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM) and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal (OMHM). It is acquiring and transferring land for social housing, and providing grants to organizations and co-operatives building affordable housing. It is also amending the by-law requiring developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the SHDM's 2026 budget; the SHDM manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units. The urban agglomeration council approves the OMHM's budget; the OMHM houses 42,587 households and plans $250M in major repairs.

The City obtains from the Government of Canada, at no cost, half of a 3,658.8-square-metre lot on rue Jolicoeur in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, and transfers, at no cost, a lot on boulevard de l'Acadie to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni. It buys a 1,535.1-square-metre lot in Le Sud-Ouest for $9,293,113 and removes eleven lots from the list of properties subject to its right of first refusal.

The executive committee approves two funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary shelter and housing search assistance. The OMHM's housing search service receives $500,000 for costs incurred from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.

Following a public consultation held on February 26, 2026, city council amends the by-law on the provision of social, affordable and family housing. The by-law now only applies to projects larger than 18,000 square metres, contributions return to 2025 amounts, and a single 20% requirement for non-market housing replaces the separate requirements.

The City provides $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for 26 units on boulevard de l'Acadie, an additional $877,312 to Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors, $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel for 350 affordable units, and $13,151,528 to Immobilier collectif – Point commun for 395 units in Pointe-Saint-Charles. The executive committee also authorizes the SHDM to build 72 units on the 2e Avenue, in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie.

aSurveiller.texte: For the 350-unit project at the Technopôle Angus, occupancy is expected by April 30, 2027 at the latest.
For the SHDM's 72-unit building on the 2e Avenue, delivery is expected in May 2028.
For the 395-unit building in Pointe-Saint-Charles, occupancy is expected in February 2030.
The Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough will incorporate the fee exemption into its 2027 local fee by-law.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary layouts.

etapes.texte: City council extended the lease of a 2,787 square-metre lot to the Société de transport de Montréal, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, for a total rent of $49,293. It also extended the lease of a neighbouring 836 square-metre lot to an app-based parking company, for $45,049 before taxes.

City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités," because the first residential project is under construction and addresses need to be assigned. The name came from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Contract for the street and soils
etapes.texte: The City awarded Charex inc. the construction of a 610-metre street with sewer, waterworks, lighting and underground electrical network, for $10,311,940.25 including taxes, and a total expenditure of $15,366,336. The contract includes the remediation of the soils of the former gas station, for which the City is adding $2,007,312.15 net through the environmental liability reserve.

The borough adopted a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a group of buildings, with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It then launched a draft by-law allowing, on part of the municipal lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, a height limit of 73 metres and a floor area ratio of 6.

etapes.titre: Redevelopment of rue de Louvain Est
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes and a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. In October, it authorized the filing of a financial assistance application to the ministère des Transports for the bike lane and sidewalks of this section.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027; the Ville en vert vegetable garden is loaned until December 31, 2027.
Îlot 84 could occupy the Esplanade lot from April 1 to October 31, 2027.
Work on rue de Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks and curbs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
Four other public places in the eco-district remain to be named before the completion of the development, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its contracts for processing food waste and its contracts related to ecocentres, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the 2025 report on the agglomeration's residual materials management.

etapes.texte: The City is extending twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanize food waste from the east of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred at Montréal-Est then processed at Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and at Moose Creek, Ontario, while waiting for the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre to come into service.

etapes.titre: Bin purchase and loan of sorting equipment
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The agglomeration extends the contracts for collecting garbage from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract of $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from the ecocentres, entrusts two firms with studies on constructions located on former waste disposal sites, and extends the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The dishware, water fountain and sorting station loan program is offered until no later than December 31, 2026.
The extension of the food waste processing contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The dumping authorization management software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It got an extra delay from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and public domain works, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline postponed to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a delay until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of public assets and funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and recreation centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and facilities in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the MultiCaf community cafeteria and the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transitional nursery. Each lease provides for a symbolic rent, and the organizations pay for development, upkeep and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The $128.3M federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031; funds from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the transfer deed to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora, and April 30, 2028 for the transitional nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.

etapes.titre: Plans and studies before the work
etapes.texte: The City entrusts the winning team of an architecture competition with the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It also pays $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil and environmental studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

The City adds $162,897.98 to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, has a culvert rebuilt at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche, and awards contracts for snow removal and the felling of ash trees and dying trees. It adds the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the registry of protected natural areas and submits Cap-Saint-Jacques's candidacy for the Urban Night Sky Place designation.

The City and the boroughs add amounts or move budgets for work already underway: monitoring of parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parcs des Hirondelles and du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray, plans for parc Percy-Walters and the museography of the parc des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne in Lachine.

City council removes a 810.2 m² section of street from the public domain to add it to parc Campbell Ouest, in Le Sud-Ouest. Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension requests the same for a 75.2 m² strip of laneway that crosses parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: City council must rule on October 19, 2026 on the removal of the laneway strip from parc Le Prévost, after it goes through the executive committee on October 7, 2026.
For the artwork at parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026 and installation in 2028.
The Grand parc de l'Ouest snow removal contract covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Final acceptance of the work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois is expected in June 2027, after the warranty year.
For the Cap-Saint-Jacques candidacy: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, and site compliance work in April 2032.
Work on parc J.O.R.-Leduc, in LaSalle, is expected to finish in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and by-laws for commercial activities.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and overseeing temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the by-laws that close the streets, authorize terraces, sales, and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a lot, and official naming.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by by-law [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee allocates $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie prohibits traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

etapes.titre: Money paid to commercial development corporations
etapes.texte: The boroughs pay contributions to the commercial development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

The borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales, and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) to local park [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite" [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The by-law on sound ambiance for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting six additional months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is reviewing its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing the heights, uses and building footprint ratio in the sector bordered by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing the allowed heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on building demolition, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent's public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the deadline granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, the date set by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its draft to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and to hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's Service de police: contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of an officer
etapes.texte: City council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized public safety equipment for the SPVM between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a sergeant-detective to the RCMP team enforcing the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City awards 9415-1966 Québec inc. the contract for meals for people detained by the SPVM and extends by one year the maintenance of the computer-aided dispatch system software with Peraton International. It leases 50 parking spaces from the Société de la Place des arts, extends the lease of the training centre in Anjou and that of neighbourhood station 15 in Verdun, and accepts $8,000 from Ottawa for a sexual assault awareness campaign.

The City enters into an agreement with Agence Gravel for 9 mm practice ammunition for firearms training, extends the SPVM's courier contract by one year and renews the lease for neighbourhood station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings, and loans a sergeant-detective to the Sûreté du Québec team on exported stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: October 23, 2026: "Fèves au lard" day of the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood station 46, for which the Anjou borough bought 62 tickets.
February 1, 2027: start of the 10-year lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood station 50, at 888, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.
March 1, 2027: deadline for delivery of the port patrol boat and its trailer.
March 31, 2027: end of the period covered by the grants from the ACCES Tabac, ACCES Alcool, ACCES Cannabis and ACCEF committees.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and loan by-laws of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then sells, leases or lends it land to expand metro stations and facilities. It also signs agreements to have municipal work carried out at the same time as work on the blue line extension, and oversees metro and REM construction sites. Some borough councils also adopt motions on network development.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council approves the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410, and its 2026-2035 capital works program [CG26 0022]. The City also enters into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, for a maximum of $41,944,604.63 including taxes, plus contingencies [CG26 0064].

etapes.titre: Land sold, leased and lent to the STM
etapes.texte: The City sells the STM a 364.3 m² piece of land near the Place-Saint-Henri station for $495,150 plus taxes [CG26 0348], land in Verdun for the Rielle ventilation station [CG26 0349], and commits to selling a portion of rue Jean-Brillant for a rectifier station [CG26 0375]. It also leases a parking lot in Ahuntsic-Cartierville to the STM [CM26 0078], lends it a small building on rue Stinson for its drivers [CE26 1303] and signs an access agreement for a piece of land on boulevard Décarie [CA26 170103].

etapes.titre: Work entrusted to the STM and bus stops
etapes.texte: The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 including taxes [CG26 0175]. It also signs an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion at parc Irma-LeVasseur, backing onto a metro ventilation station in Outremont [CM26 0198], while Ahuntsic-Cartierville sets up and removes bus waiting areas as part of the network overhaul [CA26 09 0020].

The urban agglomeration council approves several STM loans: repair of metro infrastructure, repair of surface buildings, bus priority measures, cybersecurity, extending the lifespan of MR-73 cars and analysis of their replacement. The 2026-2035 Capital Works Program is amended each time.

The City retains Artelia Canada and Stantec Experts-conseils to redevelop the blue line corridor, from Saint-Michel to Anjou, for an estimated amount of $19,070,092.68 including taxes [CG26 0564]. The city council asks Québec to study preserving the tunnel boring machine used for the blue line extension [CM26 0920]; Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring projects in the East and in the Grand Sud-Ouest, Anjou asks for the study of a reserved lane on rue Beaubien to be stopped, and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks at bus stops.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the parking lot south of rue de Louvain starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Repair and expansion work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for at most two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays; work on the bridge-tunnel is expected to continue until March 2028.
The opening of the five stations of the blue line extension is expected in 2031; the integrated municipal work is planned for 2028-2029.
The professional services agreements for the blue line corridor run from October 2026 to October 2032.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is regulating traffic around bike lanes, repairing existing sections and preparing new segments. It is also paying for maintenance contracts, settling the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths, and purchasing bikes, stations and parts for the BIXI system.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issues an ordinance that officializes bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb, between rues des Carrières and de Bellechasse, and imposes mandatory maneuvers on drivers up to rue Jean-Talon Est. Outremont files a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between avenues Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path and change parking on the north side.

City council awards a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61, taxes included, to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system, over 18 months. The executive committee then awards a contract of $394,851.17, taxes included, for the steel bases of the stations.

Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of repairs to sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as that of Ville-Marie for roadway and bike lane work. Repairs to the bike path on rue De Louvain, between rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, are also covered, for $570,000 in 2027.

City council authorizes the filing of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. Ville-Marie makes rue Saint-Jacques one-way eastbound, between rue Peel and boulevard Robert-Bourassa, for a portion of the Réseau express vélo.

aSurveiller.texte: Repairs to the bike path on rue De Louvain, between rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, are listed for $570,000 in 2027.
